question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

The Seta-Manikia dam in Evia has remained unfinished since 2005, despite being a vital project for the water supply of the municipalities of Kymi-Aliveri and Eretria, which have been affected by extremely significant drinking water shortages over time. The completion of the project will significantly improve water supply, irrigation, water resources management and the production of renewable energy, contributing decisively to the climate resilience of the wider region. According to the competent Greek authorities, the project now has updated technical studies and approved environmental conditions, but its financing decision is pending. Public reports link the project’s financing to the Island Decarbonisation Fund, with resources from the auction of 25 million CO₂ emission allowances under the European Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). However, the status of the dam’s inclusion in this financial instrument remains unclear. The Commission is asked: 1.

Has the Greek Government included the ‘Seta-Manikia’ dam in the list of projects of the Decarbonisation Fund and, if so, what are the key details of the investment (works to be financed, budget, timetable)?
In the event that the project is not included in the Decarbonisation Fund, what alternative EU financial instruments or programmes could be used to finance this dam?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.7.2026) 1. The Emissions Trading System (ETS) Greek Decarbonisation Fund provides up to 25 million allowances for decarbonisation of the electricity supply of Greek islands. As the decarbonisation project is undergoing assessment by the European Investment Bank (EIB), as per the terms set out in Article 10a(9) of the ETS Directive1, the Commission is not in a position to share information on the project components at this stage. Information on the project components supported under the Greek Decarbonisation Fund will be made publicly available once the project has been confirmed. 2. If the dam project is not financed under the Decarbonisation Fund, other funds could serve as the main EU financing instrument. In fact, EU funding has supported investments in Greece across a range of sectors, including dam infrastructure. For instance, the Recovery and Resilience Facility has supported projects such as the Amfilochia pumped-storage hydropower plant in Western Greece, with an EU contribution of around EUR 250 million2. Moreover, under the 2021-2027 period, approximately EUR 2.1 billion has been allocated under Cohesion Policy funds in Greece to support secure access to drinking water, sustainable water management, and resilient public water supply and wastewater infrastructure. Under Cohesion Policy and in accordance with the principle of shared management, Member States are responsible for the selection and implementation of projects, including water-related investments, in line with programme priorities and Regulations3.
1 Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003 establishing a scheme

for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC. 2 European Commission, Reforms and Investments: Pumped Storage Hydro Plant in Western Greece (Amfilochia). Additional information available in the link: https://reformsinvestments.ec.europa.eu/projects/pumped-storage-hydro-plant-western-greece-amfilochia_en. 3 Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 June 2021.
